_readme: Original-wording FAQs. 'confirm' means the answer depends on business-specific facts to verify with the client. Insurance answers follow Texas Department of Insurance guidance.

items.q: How do I get a quote?
items.a: Book an inspection online. We look at the whole roof system, document what we find, then walk you through repair and replacement options.

items.q: Is the inspection free?
items.a: The business advertises free inspections and estimates. Confirm any limits (area, type of property) before publishing.

items.q: How does online booking work?
items.a: Choose a service, pick an open time, enter your details and confirm. Sign in with Google or your phone number so you can see your appointment and project progress any time.

items.q: Can I reschedule or cancel?
items.a: Yes. You can change or cancel from your dashboard up to 24 hours before your appointment.

items.q: How long does a roof replacement take?
items.a: Most home replacements take one to two days on site, depending on roof size, complexity and weather. Larger or multi-building jobs are scheduled in phases.

items.q: What happens before work starts?
items.a: We inspect, confirm scope and options, check permit and HOA requirements, order materials and schedule the install. Each step shows on your project timeline.

items.q: How will I know what is happening?
items.a: Your dashboard shows the current stage, notes and photos from our team, and a history of every update.

items.q: Do I need a full replacement?
items.a: Not always. Isolated damage can often be repaired. Widespread wear, storm damage or age may make replacement the better long-term choice. We show you both paths.

items.q: Why do Houston roofs get replaced so often?
items.a: Heat, UV, humidity, wind and hail all age roofs here, and insurance requirements often influence timing as well. Age, storm history and current condition drive the decision.

items.q: What does an inspection cover?
items.a: Shingles, flashing, ventilation, penetrations and common trouble spots, plus the attic where accessible. You get a clear list of what needs attention now versus later.

items.q: Why is my insurer asking me to replace a roof that is not leaking?
items.a: Insurers can set requirements based on roof age or storm history. Read your notice carefully and ask your insurer or agent what applies to your policy.

items.q: Do you handle my insurance claim?
items.a: No. In Texas a roofer cannot act as your public adjuster while also doing the work. We document the damage with photos and a written report that you can share with your insurer. You file and manage your own claim.

items.q: Will you cover my deductible?
items.a: No. Texas law prohibits contractors from waiving, rebating or absorbing a deductible. You owe the deductible to the contractor.

items.q: How long does my insurer have to respond?
items.a: Per Texas Department of Insurance guidance, an insurer has 15 business days to acknowledge a claim, and once it agrees to pay it has five business days to get payment started. Check the TDI page for current details.

items.q: Should I get more than one bid?
items.a: Yes. TDI recommends getting bids from several contractors when choosing who repairs your roof.

items.q: Does a bigger warranty number mean a better roof?
items.a: Not by itself. Correct installation, proper warranty registration and coverage that fits how long you will own the property matter more than the headline number.

items.q: What warranty will I get?
items.a: TODO: confirm exact manufacturer and workmanship warranty names, terms and years with the client.

items.q: Do you push one brand?
items.a: The business says it is manufacturer-neutral and presents options across systems. Confirm which manufacturers it installs.

items.q: Does Texas license roofers?
items.a: No. Texas does not require a state roofing license. RCAT offers a voluntary license, which the business states it holds.

items.q: What is GAF Master Elite?
items.a: A top contractor tier from GAF, the largest U.S. shingle maker. Certified contractors can offer GAF's strongest manufacturer warranties. You can verify a contractor on GAF's website.

items.q: Do you use subcontractors?
items.a: The business says its project managers are in-house employees and that it does not subcontract roof projects. Confirm before publishing.

items.q: How do you work around tenants and operations?
items.a: We plan phased schedules, controlled access and clear communication with property managers.

items.q: Where do we start for a commercial property?
items.a: With an inspection or walkthrough. It shows current condition and helps decide whether to replace now, repair, or plan for later.
